title: Grateful Dead Live at Monterey Fairgrounds on 1967-06-18
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT x 2 > Sonic Solutions > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of Monterey’s historic set – high‑energy Viola Lee Blues, Alligator and Caution shine despite occasional harmonica mishaps.
ai_review.review: The recording is a surprisingly clean soundboard source that places the listener right in the 1967 Monterey Pop Festival, with a crisp mix and enough ambience to feel the massive crowd. Musically the Dead deliver an electrifying short set – Viola Lee Blues erupts, Alligator rolls into a fiery Caution, and even a shaky Cold Rain & Snow can't dampen the overall excitement, though the off‑key harmonica moments draw criticism.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate 4–5 stars, praising historic importance and strong performances; technical flaws are noted but do not dominate, yielding a solid combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clean for a 1967 tape – crisp stereo image, occasional mic drop‑outs (Pigpen's early harmonica), minor glitches and a few out‑of‑key moments, but overall listenable and well balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, high‑energy set that bursts from the opening Viola Lee into Alligator and rolls straight into Caution; despite technical hiccups the pacing stays tight and the crowd’s excitement is palpable.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is repeatedly praised as wild, out‑of‑control and high‑energy, though one reviewer notes occasional tuning slippage.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals are generally called ‘awesome’ but no specific comments about Weir’s playing appear.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work on Caution is highlighted as powerful; his early harmonica is criticized for being off‑key and possibly not even Pigpen.
